Order.description:
One order: what to pay, where, and how far the payment has got.

Its status moves from `pending` through `unconfirmed` and `confirming`
to `paid` (or `partial`, `overpaid`, `expired`); `is_final` says it
won't change again. Follow `mk:order-events` to hear each change as it
happens, and send the payer to `mk:checkout`.

problems.doc:
The request carried no key, or one this Monokulo doesn't know: a
mistyped key, a secret key that has since been replaced (the store's
plugin was disconnected and connected again), or an app that was
disconnected. Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` with a current key.
problems.title: No valid key

problems.doc:
The key is valid but may not do this: each route says which keys it
takes. A store's public key (`pk_`) only makes and reads orders;
only an app's own key (`ak_`) reads or disconnects the app; only the
store's secret key (`sk_`) sends a plugin's logs. A store that takes
orders only from its verified websites also refuses an order made
with its public key anywhere else.
problems.title: Not allowed with this key

problems.doc:
There's no such order for the store the key names. An order of
another store is not found either.
problems.title: Not found

problems.doc:
The request body isn't what the form takes: not JSON, a field
missing or of the wrong type, or a value its rules refuse (`detail`
says which). The form in `_templates` lists every field and its
rules.
problems.title: Invalid request

problems.doc: The body was sent without `Content-Type: application/json`.
problems.title: Send JSON

problems.doc:
The order can't be priced: the currency is unknown, this Monokulo
has no exchange rate for it right now, or the amount isn't one the
currency can have.
problems.title: The order can't be priced

problems.doc:
The `idempotency_key` was used before for a different order: a
different amount, currency or reference.
problems.title: Key used for another order

problems.doc: The request body is larger than the route takes.
problems.title: Request too large

problems.doc:
The store hasn't turned on client logs, so its plugin's reports are
refused. The merchant turns them on in the store's settings.
problems.title: Client logs are off for this store

problems.doc:
Too many requests from this client. Wait `retry_after` seconds (also
in the `Retry-After` header) before trying again.
problems.title: Too many requests

problems.doc:
Too many requests from this connection: solve the challenge in
`challenge` (find a nonce such that SHA-256 of the challenge
followed by the nonce starts with `difficulty` zero bits) and send
the request again with `Monokulo-Proof: <challenge>.<nonce>`. The
embed library does this by itself.
problems.title: Solve a challenge to continue

problems.doc:
This client has as many live update streams open for the store as
it may. Close one first.
problems.title: Too many open streams

problems.doc:
The payment engine is busy or can't be reached. Try again in a
moment.
problems.title: Payment engine unavailable

problems.doc:
The store's settings can't be read right now. Try again in a
moment.
problems.title: Store unavailable

problems.doc:
Something went wrong on this Monokulo. Its admin can find it in the
logs; try again later.
problems.title: Internal error

resources.description:
The store's sale events, as server-sent events: one stream for all its orders.

It starts with `ready`; then each sale event is an `event:` named after it (`sale.waiting`, `sale.paid`, `sale.expired`, ...) with its JSON as data. `lagged` means some were missed: read the orders again. A connected app's stream ends when the app is disconnected.

methods.doc:
Make an order.

With the store's secret key or an app's (a shop's server, a till) it is
recorded as made with the key; with the public key it's the website's,
and a store that takes orders only from its verified websites refuses it
from anywhere else. A shop plugin names itself in `Monokulo-Client:
<slug>/<version>`. Answers `201 Created` with the order and its
`Location`.

resources.description:
One order's changes, as server-sent events.

An `order` event carries the order (the same JSON as reading it) each time it changes, and every 30 seconds as its time to pay runs down; the stream ends once the order is final, after a last `order` event. `done` with `not_found` ends it for an order that's gone.
